summary: MotionAlert app tested end-to-end. Backend 4/4 pytest passing (root Hello World + Mongo status GET/POST/validation). Frontend web preview loaded on 375x667 mobile viewport; permission-screen path validated via code review (CDP auto-grants camera on web preview, so live-feed-screen rendered directly). All 9 required testIDs on the live-feed screen are present with correct initial values: status-text=STANDBY, sensitivity-value=60%, toggle-monitor-button label=START. Toggle transitions verified: START→STOP flips status to MONITORING, STOP→START returns to STANDBY. Sensitivity slider is interactive via drag (60%→12%→93%). No red screen errors, no page errors, TypeScript builds and expo service healthy.

issues: Deprecation warning: props.pointerEvents is deprecated; move to style.pointerEvents on LinearGradient/reticleWrap/statusPillWrap (non-blocking, react-native-web v0.19+).

action_items: OPTIONAL: Replace `pointerEvents` prop with `style={{ pointerEvents: 'none' }}` on LinearGradient/View wrappers to silence RN-web deprecation warnings.

NOTE: Live camera frame diff + TTS motion-detection logic cannot be exercised in the Playwright/web harness (CDP fake camera returns a static pattern). Requires a physical device / Expo Go to validate motion + TTS behaviour.
critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx cleanly separates permission gating from live feed; refs guard against stale closures (isMonitoringRef, sensitivityRef).
AppState listener stops monitoring on background - good.
processFrame swallows transient errors silently; consider a dev-only console.warn when jpeg.decode fails to aid future debugging.
TTS_COOLDOWN_MS=4000 and motion reset 1500ms are sensible defaults.
seed_data_creation: One TEST_<uuid8> status record inserted via test_status_create_and_persist (harmless test-prefixed data).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Web preview auto-grants camera via CDP so permission-screen may not render by default; to test the permission screen, revoke via `page.context.clear_permissions()` before goto. Slider on web uses a custom div (role=slider) - drive it with mouse.down/move/up over its bounding box, not by setting an <input type=range>.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no bugs found. All acceptance criteria met.
